# Paired maximum depth: local and global simplex stability

This is ordinary continuous geometry, not mixed-integer OC. The strict
nonzero-shift centroid equality lemma and paired equality rigidity are
now proved in `candidate d494e7e71949ac0b`; root has
read and checked that complete proof. No conclusion here is imported
into a mixed-center argument.

For an ordinary full-dimensional convex body K in R^d define

    P_K(y)=inf_(|u|=1,s>=0)
       [|K intersect{u.(x-y)>=s}|+|K intersect{u.(x-y)>=-s}|]/(2|K|),
    P(K)=max_(y in K) P_K(y),
    Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d.

The archived paired-centroid theorem gives P_K(g_K)>=Gamma and therefore
P(K)>=Gamma. At s=0 the quantity is ordinary halfspace depth in direction
u, so P(K)<=D(K). In particular P(S)=Gamma for every simplex S.

The quantity is invariant under invertible ordinary affine maps. Under
x'=Lx+b and y'=Ly+b, an original unit normal and shift become

    u'=L^(-T)u/|L^(-T)u|, s'=s/|L^(-T)u|.

The two halfspaces remain a paired through-center family, and the
inverse map gives the converse correspondence. All volumes multiply
by one determinant, which cancels in the normalized fraction. This
statement concerns ordinary continuous bodies only.

## 1. Compactness and continuity

Suppose all bodies under consideration lie in the Euclidean ball R B_d,
and centers y lie there too. Then s>=2R makes one cap full and the other
null, up to a supporting hyperplane of zero d-volume. The paired fraction
is1/2 there. Since the infimum is at most1/2 (opposite through-point caps
sum to full measure), the parameter domain may be restricted to the
compact set |u|=1,0<=s<=2R.

For one fixed positive-volume body, both cap masses are jointly continuous
in u,s,y: indicators converge off a hyperplane of zero d-volume, and
dominated convergence applies. Thus the paired infimum is attained and
is continuous in y on a compact region. Its maximum on K is attained.

If K_l converge in Hausdorff distance to a full-dimensional convex K,
with a common bounding ball, their uniform probabilities converge in total
variation. This bounds the change of EVERY paired functional by that
same total variation error, because each paired functional is the average
of two halfspace probabilities. A center displacement of size h changes
each cap by at most the volume of a width-h slab in the bounding ball,
at most kappa_(d-1)R^(d-1)h before normalization. Volume is bounded below
along such a sequence. These estimates prove uniform center continuity.
Approximating a limiting maximizing center, and taking a subsequence of
maximizing centers, give P(K_l)->P(K). No selected minimizing cap or
maximizing center is assumed to vary continuously.

## 2. The proved equality input used locally

For a standard simplex S in dimension d>=3, with centroid g, the needed
statement is

    the only pairs (u,s) with paired fraction Gamma at g
    have s=0 and u an apex-side facet-parallel canonical normal.          (E)

The ordinary part at s=0 is proved in
`candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c`. The positive-shift
part follows from Sections1-4 of
`candidate d494e7e71949ac0b`: EVERY centered
convex-body marginal in d>=3 has strictly larger paired fraction at
each fixed s>0. That proof uses an ACTUAL maximizing extremizer on a
fixed compact interval in the standard one-constraint localization
theorem, then proves strictness for every permitted extremizer. It does
not substitute pointwise strictness over an unclosed family for (E).

## 3. Relative local stability

Let d>=3, m=d+1 and

    c=[1-d^(1-d)]/[(d-1)^2(d+1)]>0.

There exists delta_d>0 such that if

    (1-delta)S+delta g_S subset K subset S,
    delta<=delta_d,
    every facet centroid of S belongs to K,

then the actual point constructed below satisfies

    P_K(y)-Gamma >=(Gamma c/4)(1-|K|/|S|).                   (1)

By that affine invariance, normalize S to the STANDARD simplex
conv(0,e_1,...,e_d) before making ANY choice of parameter neighborhoods,
bounding ball, or compact gap. Thus all constants selected below depend
only on d. We give the proof and every change required from the already audited
ordinary local theorem `candidate c62d1cc13c75171f`.
All radial gauge, facet-functional and weighted strip lemmas in Sections
1-4 of that source apply unchanged. Set tau=1-|K|/|S| and use its constants

    C=8m, eta=min{1/(8m),Gamma c/[4C2^(d+1)]}, E=C eta2^(d+1),
    R_i=|(S minus K) intersect{lambda_i>=1/m}|/|S|,
    L_i=min{tau,R_i+E tau}, Lbar=(1/m)sum_i L_i.

For delta<=min(1/2,c/(4d)), the proved facet and strip estimates give

    Lbar<=Gamma(1-c/2)tau.                                  (2)

They also give missing volume at most L_i|S| for EVERY halfspace whose
affine margin differs from lambda_i-1/m by at most eta on S. In
particular this estimate may be applied separately to TWO nearby cap
thresholds; no through-center restriction entered the strip proof.

Fix a ball bounding S and a small center neighborhood; let Q be the
compact parameter domain of Section1. By (E) the paired fraction at g
has precisely m minimizing parameters (u_i,0). Choose small disjoint
relative open neighborhoods U_i in Q. Choose chi>0 small enough that,
whenever |lambda_j(y)-1/m|<=chi and (u,s) is in U_i, BOTH margins

    |grad lambda_i|[u.(x-y)-s],
    |grad lambda_i|[u.(x-y)+s]

differ from lambda_i(x)-1/m by at most eta on S. They can also be
chosen so that each cap isolates exactly vertex i. All vertex signs
are strict at (u_i,0,g), so these are genuine open neighborhood
conditions. Compactness and (E) give a gap rho0>0 on Q outside the
U_i. Shrink chi so that for every such parameter and every indicated
center, the paired S fraction is at least Gamma+rho0/2.

Choose ONE center by

    lambda_i(y)=1/m+(Lbar-L_i)/(m Gamma).                    (3)

For tau<=Gamma/2 and delta<=1/4 these coordinates are at least1/(2m),
strictly greater than delta/m. Thus y lies inside the inner simplex
and hence inside K. For tau<=m Gamma chi it also lies in the prescribed
center neighborhood.

For a parameter in U_i, fix u and write h=u.(v_i-y)>0. Since the two
caps both isolate vertex i, their S volumes have the exact form

    A_u(h-s)^d and A_u(h+s)^d,

with the same positive coefficient A_u, independent of s. This follows
from the edge-intercept determinant formula; all d intercept numerators
are h-s or h+s, and their edge denominators depend only on u and S.
Both h-s and h+s are positive. Convexity of the dth power gives

    [A_u(h-s)^d+A_u(h+s)^d]/2 >= A_u h^d.                  (4)

The right side is the ordinary through-y cap. The same determinant
formula and AM-GM therefore give the lower fraction
d^d product_(j!=i)lambda_j(y). By the finite product estimate already
proved in the ordinary source, with B=2^d/Gamma, this is at least

    Gamma-m Gamma[lambda_i(y)-1/m]-B tau^2.

Each of the two missing-volume terms is at most L_i|S|, so their average
is also at most L_i|S|. Equations(2)-(4) give a paired K fraction,
measured relative to |S|, at least

    Gamma-Lbar-B tau^2
       >=Gamma-Gamma(1-c/2)tau-B tau^2.                     (5)

For parameters outside the U_i, the paired S fraction is at least
Gamma+rho0/2. Each missing fraction is at most tau, so their average
is at most tau. If tau<=rho0/4, this lower bound is greater than Gamma
and hence also implies(5). Larger shifts outside Q give fraction1/2
and do not reduce the infimum.

Finally divide(5) by1-tau. If tau<=Gamma c/(4B), the improvement over
Gamma is at least Gamma c tau/4, proving(1). One admissible choice is

    tau*=min{Gamma/2,m Gamma chi,rho0/4,Gamma c/(4B)},
    delta_d=min{1/4,c/(4d),tau*/d}.

The inner-simplex inclusion gives tau<=d delta, verifying every bound.
If tau=0, K=S and its centroid gives equality separately. This proves
the relative local theorem using the proved input(E).

## 4. Local Hausdorff and global consequences

The attained minimum enclosing simplex, its facet-centroid contacts,
and its quantitative near-simplex locality are already proved. Section6
of the ordinary local theorem consequently applies verbatim with the
new positive delta_d: every sufficiently close ordinary convex body has
an enclosing minimizer S to which(1) applies. Thus the local estimate
requires no new shape approximation or convergence argument.

The further equality-rigidity theorem, proved in Sections5-6 of the
same rigidity source, states

    P(K)=Gamma implies K is a simplex                         (R)

Consequently there is also a finite dimension-only A_d such that EVERY
ordinary convex body in dimension d>=3 and EVERY minimum enclosing
simplex S obey

    1-|K|/|S| <= A_d[P(K)-Gamma].                            (6)

Indeed normalize by an attained maximum-volume inscribed simplex.
The archived ordinary global proof confines the normalized body to
one fixed barycentric polytope and proves compactness. Every normalized
simplex in that class is the reference simplex itself. Section1 gives
continuity of P; (R) gives a strictly positive attained minimum of
P-Gamma on the closed complement of the local neighborhood. If that
complement is empty, take its gap as1. Combining its reciprocal with
the local coefficient4/(Gamma c) proves(6), since the left side is
at most1. This repeats no unproved selection or minimizer assumption.

Thus both local and global estimates have complete proved dependencies.
The original proof notes retain the ordinary measure, paired-cap
parameter, actual continuous center, and compactness arguments. None
selects a mixed-integer center or proves the general OC claim.
